# Domain Rules

<!-- Generated by /ai-context. Manual edits are overwritten on re-run. -->

## AS IS — Current state

### Overview

- **Offline-first event lifecycle**: Local, iCloud, CalDAV, ICS subscription, and contact birthday/anniversary events reside in Room (`KashCalDatabase.kt`), while device-calendar events stay in `CalendarProvider` and Tasks.org tasks stay in `org.tasks.api` (`EventCoordinator.kt`, `DisplayEventRepository.kt`).
- **Materialized recurrence**: Recurring rules (`RRULE`, `RDATE`, `EXDATE`) are expanded ahead of time into `occurrences` rows for indexed $O(1)$ day/range queries (`OccurrenceGenerator.kt`, `RRuleExpander.kt`).
- **Queue-driven two-way sync**: Synced calendar mutations queue `PendingOperation` rows drained before pulling server deltas (`CalDavSyncEngine.kt`, `PendingOperation.kt`).
- **Gated fork extensions**: Tasks.org integration (`// FORK:tasks-org`), Travel Time departure alerts (`// FORK:travel-time`), and automatic settings/calendar backups (`// FORK:auto-backup`) operate as opt-in overlays controlled by `KashCalDataStore` toggles (`docs/fork/FORK_INTEGRATION.md`).

### Master and Exception Recurrence Model (RFC 5545)

Implemented in `Event.kt`, `Occurrence.kt`, `EventWriter.kt`, `OccurrenceGenerator.kt`, and `RRuleExpander.kt`:
- A recurring series has one master `Event` row (`rrule != null`, `originalEventId == null`) enforced unique per `(calendar_id, uid)` by SQLite triggers `trigger_master_event_unique_insert` and `trigger_master_event_unique_update` (`KashCalDatabase.kt` lines 158-189).
- Editing a single occurrence creates an exception `Event` row that shares the master's `uid`, sets `originalEventId = master.id`, sets `originalInstanceTime` to the replaced occurrence's `RECURRENCE-ID` timestamp, and uses `importId = "{uid}:RECID:{datetime}"` (`Event.kt` lines 55-66, 170-180).
- `OccurrenceGenerator.generateOccurrences` expands `RecurrenceSet = (DTSTART ∪ RRULE ∪ RDATE) - EXDATE` via `:icaldav-core` (`RRuleExpander.kt`) over a default 24-month forward window (`DEFAULT_EXPANSION_MONTHS = 24`) and relinks existing `exceptionEventId` references within a 60-second tolerance (`OccurrenceGenerator.kt` lines 18-33, 81-84).
- Deleting a single occurrence adds its timestamp to the master's `exdate`, deletes any exception row, and sets `Occurrence.isCancelled = true` (`Occurrence.kt` lines 76-82).
- Orphan exceptions pulled without a master attach to a synthetic master marked with `extraProperties["X-KASHCAL-SYNTHETIC-MASTER"] = "true"`, which generates 0 occurrences of its own (`OccurrenceGenerator.kt` lines 54-60).

### Scheduling Significance and `SEQUENCE` Bumping (RFC 5546)

Implemented in `SequenceBumper.kt` (lines 30-56):
- Organizer edits increment `Event.sequence` by 1 only when a scheduling-significant field changes: `startTs`, `endTs`, `isAllDay`, `duration`, semantic `rrule` (`RruleUtils.rrulesEquivalent`), `rdate`, `exdate`, transition of `status` to `"CANCELLED"`, trimmed `title`, or trimmed `location`.
- Cosmetic edits (notes/description, categories, color, reminders) preserve `sequence` so attendees are not re-notified.

### CalDAV Sync Order, Queue Lifetimes, and Conflict Resolution

Implemented in `CalDavSyncEngine.kt`, `PendingOperation.kt`, `PendingOperationTriggers.kt`, `PushStrategy.kt`, `PullStrategy.kt`, and `ConflictResolver.kt`:
- Per writable calendar, `CalDavSyncEngine.syncCalendar` runs in strict order: (1) `pushStrategy.pushForCalendar`, (2) `conflictResolver.resolve` for failed operations, (3) `pullStrategy.pull` (`CalDavSyncEngine.kt` lines 35-38, 104-194).
- Local edits protect rows from being overwritten during pull: `Event.hasPendingChanges()` returns `true` when `syncStatus` is `PENDING_CREATE`, `PENDING_UPDATE`, or `PENDING_DELETE` (`Event.kt` lines 400-414).
- `PendingOperation` retries use exponential backoff `30s * 2^retryCount` capped at 5 hours (`MAX_BACKOFF_MS`) for up to `maxRetries = 10` (`PendingOperation.kt` lines 49-50, 187-204). Operations failed for >24 hours (`AUTO_RESET_FAILED_MS`) auto-reset to `PENDING` until their 30-day `OPERATION_LIFETIME_MS` expires, after which they transition to `STATUS_ABANDONED` (`PendingOperation.kt` lines 174-190).
- On HTTP `412 Precondition Failed`, `ConflictResolver` attempts resolution up to `MAX_CONFLICT_SYNC_CYCLES = 3` cycles before abandoning the local change in favor of the server copy and posting a notification (`CalDavSyncEngine.kt` lines 57-62, 133-153).
- Same-account calendar moves start at `MOVE_PHASE_DELETE = 0` (WebDAV `MOVE` with `Overwrite: F`) and fall back to `MOVE_PHASE_CREATE = 1` (`CREATE` in target with a fresh retry budget, then `DELETE` in source). Cross-account moves pair a `CREATE` and `DELETE` via `linkedMoveId` so `getReadyOperations()` holds the source `DELETE` until the target `CREATE` finishes (`PendingOperation.kt` lines 78-89, 119-128).

### Calendar Muting vs Visibility

Implemented in `Calendar.kt`, `EventCoordinator.kt`, and `TravelAlarmWorker.kt`:
- Hiding a calendar (`Calendar.isVisible = false`) hides its events from UI views but keeps all scheduled reminders armed (`Calendar.kt` lines 61-63, 80-81).
- Muting a calendar (`Calendar.isNotificationMuted = true`) keeps events visible and synced in `RecentChange`, but suppresses event reminders, travel departure alerts, invitation notifications, and background-sync change notifications (`Calendar.kt` lines 77-84, `TravelAlarmWorker.kt` lines 84-88).

### Tasks.org Integration, VTODO Filtering & All-Day View Stacking Rules (`// FORK:tasks-org`)

Implemented in `DisplayEventRepository.kt`, `TasksOrgCoordinator.kt`, `TasksOrgVTodoFilter.kt`, `TasksOrgV0Mapper.kt`, `TasksOrgBatch.kt`, `AgendaListModel.kt`, `AllDayStripLayout.kt`, `PlannerView.kt`, and `MonthFullSpanLayout.kt`:
- **Master gate**: `DisplayEventRepository.queryTaskEvents` returns `emptyList()` when `KashCalDataStore.tasksOrgEnabled` is false; when disabled, no `ContentObserver` is registered and no `org.tasks.permission.*` permissions are requested (`TasksOrgCoordinator.kt` lines 67-73).
- **Non-persistence & timezone convention**: Tasks are never written to Room (`AGENTS.md`). All-day due/start dates are converted to UTC midnight on read (to align with KashCal day codes) and local midnight on write (matching Tasks.org convention) (`docs/fork/FORK_FEATURES.md` §10).
- **Device Calendar VTODO filtering**: When `tasksOrgEnabled` is true and read permission is granted, `TasksOrgVTodoFilter.filterDeviceCalendars` omits `DeviceCalendar` entries whose normalized `(accountName.trim().lowercase(), displayName.trim().lowercase())` tuple matches a Tasks.org `(account.name, list.title)` tuple, preventing empty VTODO task collections from cluttering the device calendar list (`TasksOrgVTodoFilter.kt` lines 14-65, `docs/fork/FORK_FEATURES.md` §15).
- **Overdue & future recurring occurrences**: Overdue tasks stay on their scheduled due date rather than rolling to today (`docs/fork/FORK_FEATURES.md` §2.1). Open recurring tasks with `repeat_from = "due_date"` expand up to 400 future read-only occurrences (`◌` prefix, max 1 per day, 366-day lookback `FUTURE_OCCURRENCE_LOOKBACK_MS`); completing a future occurrence is refused (`TasksOrgCoordinator.kt` line 89).
- **Recurrence preservation & side-effect detection**: Rules that the KashCal task editor cannot build are preserved verbatim without `RRULE:` prefix (`normalizeRule` in `TasksOrgCoordinator.kt` line 206). When a recurring task's due date changes without editing its rule, `TasksOrgCoordinator.updateTask` re-reads the task from Tasks.org and flags `TasksOrgSaveOutcome.recurrenceAdjusted = true` if Tasks.org rewrote the rule (`TasksOrgCoordinator.kt` lines 150-164).
- **Atomic batch saves**: Creating or updating a task executes a single `ContentResolver.applyBatch` plan (`TasksOrgBatch.kt`) covering task columns, new/linked tags via back-references, reminders, and places (`TasksOrgCoordinator.kt` lines 137-163).
- **All-day event & task stacking across views**: In Agenda, Day Drawer, Planner (`PlannerView.kt`), Week/3-Day/Day all-day strips (`AllDayStripLayout.kt`), and Full-Height Month (`MonthFullSpanLayout.kt`), single-day all-day events (`> 1`) and all-day tasks (`> 1`) consolidate into separate expandable summary cards/ribbons/chips (`EventGroupSummary` and `TaskGroupSummary`), while multi-day spans and singletons (`== 1`) render individually (`docs/fork/FORK_INTEGRATION.md` §2).

### Travel Time Estimation & Routing Cascade (`// FORK:travel-time`)

Implemented in `RoutingService.kt`, `RouteCache.kt`, `CircuitBreaker.kt`, `RushHourEstimator.kt`, `TravelReminderScheduler.kt`, and `TravelAlarmWorker.kt`:
- `TravelReminderScheduler` enqueues a unique `TravelAlarmWorker` 1 hour (`LEAD_TIME_MS = 3_600_000L`) before each occurrence of a timed event (`!isAllDay`) that has a non-null `Event.travelMode` (`CAR`, `FOOT`, `TRANSIT`) (`TravelReminderScheduler.kt` lines 56-98).
- `TravelAlarmWorker` resolves destination coordinates from `(Event.geoLat, Event.geoLon)` or geocodes `Event.location`, resolves origin coordinates from `Event.travelOriginFixed` or live AOSP `LocationManager` via `TravelLocationProvider`, and queries `RoutingService.estimate` (`TravelAlarmWorker.kt` lines 90-123).
- `RoutingService` evaluates sources in strict cascade order and never fails (`RoutingService.kt` lines 41-67):

| Priority | Source (`RoutingSource`) | Enabled Condition | Circuit Breaker Skip Condition | Live Traffic | Post-Processing Margin | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `RouteCache` (in-memory LRU, 64 max) | Always checked first | Entry older than `TTL_MS` (15 min) | Preserved from cached `RoutingResult` | Already applied | Returns cached `RoutingResult` (`RouteCache.kt` lines 40-61). |
| 1 | `TOMTOM` (`TomTomRoutingProvider`) | `travelTomTomEnabled && apiKey.isNotBlank()` | `CircuitBreaker.isOpen(TOMTOM)` | `true` for `CAR`/`TRANSIT`, `false` for `FOOT` | `+10 min` (`TRANSIT_OVERHEAD_MIN`) if `TRANSIT` | Caches and returns result (`TomTomRoutingProvider.kt` lines 32-66). |
| 2 | `STADIA` (`StadiaMapsProvider`) | `travelStadiaEnabled && apiKey.isNotBlank()` | `CircuitBreaker.isOpen(STADIA)` | `false` | `+10 min` if `TRANSIT`; `+30%` rush-hour margin if `CAR` on weekday 07:30–09:30 or 17:30–19:30 | Caches and returns result (`StadiaMapsProvider.kt` lines 30-55, `RushHourEstimator.kt` lines 15-29). |
| 3 | `VALHALLA` (`ValhallaDemoProvider`) | `travelValhallaEnabled` | `CircuitBreaker.isOpen(VALHALLA)` | `false` | `+10 min` if `TRANSIT`; `+30%` rush-hour margin if `CAR` on weekday peak | Caches and returns result (`ValhallaDemoProvider.kt` lines 30-50). |
| 4 | `LOCAL` (`LocalHaversineProvider`) | Always enabled (offline fallback) | Never skipped | `false` | `+30%` rush-hour margin if `CAR` on weekday peak | Returns offline Haversine distance × `tortuosityFactor` / `speedKmh` (`LocalHaversineProvider.kt` lines 16-27). |

- **Circuit breaker transitions** (`CircuitBreaker.kt` lines 42-80): HTTP `429` (`RoutingRateLimitedException`) opens the breaker immediately for 15 minutes (`COOLDOWN_MS`); HTTP `401`/`403` (`RoutingAuthException`) opens it immediately for 60 minutes (`BAD_KEY_COOLDOWN_MS`); 2 consecutive transport/5xx failures (`FAILURES_BEFORE_OPEN = 2`) open it for 15 minutes.
- To add a new online routing provider, implement `RoutingProvider` (`source`, `isEnabled()`, `estimate(...)`) and register it in `RoutingService`'s `@Inject` constructor list (`RoutingService.kt` lines 27-35).
